## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore the bundled defaults before merge because their deletion breaks the existing loader; port validation and configuration error reporting also need correction. Tests were read, not run.

## Changes
Adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, host normalization, and tests. Deletes the bundled defaults and adds reviewer documentation and a hostile-text fixture.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore the defaults required by the existing loader — Calling `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`: app/startup.py:6 still reads the deleted `defaults.json`. — Users invoking the existing defaults loader encounter a failure instead of receiving the bundled timeout configuration.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False` because the comparison excludes the documented upper endpoint of the usable port range. — Callers using this validator reject a valid TCP port.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Preserve configuration failure information — Loading malformed JSON or an unreadable file returns `{}` because `except Exception` discards parsing and filesystem errors without logging or an adjacent fallback explanation. — Users cannot distinguish a failed configuration load from a successfully loaded empty configuration or identify the underlying problem.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Cover trailing-dot host normalization — For `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`, the trailing-dot removal branch has no test coverage; the sole normalization test uses `"Example.COM"`. — Removing or breaking suffix stripping would leave the current normalization test passing. — Fix: Extend `test_normalize_host_lowercases` with a trailing-dot input.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Align the empty-host documentation and return value — For `normalize_host("")`, the docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but line 37 executes `return ""`. — Callers following the documented contract can check for `None` and miss the actual empty-host result.
